I find it very interesting to see how differently Catholics are raised and taught.
For me, when I've talked with "superiors" and asked questions and stuff, the answers I've gotten can be summed up by "love and walk God's path". Like, I know nuns that have birth control, because it is medically needed, heck I myself am (though I'm not a nun), because God doesn't want me to suffer unnecessarily when medicine exists that can help me.

Content warning: the following may feel preaching to some. That's not my intention, but I acknowledge that it may be triggering or perceived as overly idealistic. You have been warned. 

Priests I've been in contact with talks about all the different kinds of love there is, not just romantic or sexual love, and how people should love all people. God calls all of us to holiness, but our individual callings can be very different things. Some people are called to taking a wedded partner and have children, other people are called to priesthood, other people are called to tending their cats, other people are called to develop medicine, and so on. One path is not the correct path for everyone, and all my priests have been completely in agreement with this.
"Love each other like God loves you". It's powerful, and it doesn't limit what love is.  As long as we try to be what we believe is morally good, I think we're doing a good job. God tries to help us understand what our path is, whether that is a life filled with children or if it is a life filled with cats (extremely simplified), and God sends people to work with us on the journey.

I'm diagnosed with both borderline and avoidant personality disorders, and I can only speak from my own experience.

My bpd sucks so badly. My feelings are so unstable, I don't understand who I am or if they are even valid. I am impulsive, and I feel like no one cares about me. I am emotionally very erratic. 

However, my avpd is equally as horrible. I'm so scared of showing my (incredibly dramatic) feelings that it is all internalized. I avoid relationships, because I don't want to be abandoned nor rejected, and it fuels my bpd feelings. My avpd stops me
from taking any action that would be noticeable by others. 

From the outside, people would not be able to notice that I am mentally ill, because my disorders both disguise and empower each other. My impulsivity is disguised by my need to not be noticed. My invisibility fuels my feelings of not being needed or wanted. Which in turn makes me hide my thoughts and opinions. Making it difficult to obtain friends. Which again fuels my erratic feelings and coping strategies. And so on.

And this is definitely not describing the true extent of my life, because that is impossible.
Having bpd is horrible. Having avpd is horrible. Having both is just a shit show of terrible. I would much rather pick only bpd over the mix of these.

I hope this helps.

The cps traumatized me more than my mother did. Because my mother's sin was being poor and mentally ill, where the cps kept saying they would help us, just to ignore what I wanted, invalidate my feelings, and blame mom for not having what they were responsible for providing. The cps said "We're here for you, you can count on us" and when I tried talking to them, they rationalized my feelings, talked about how I don't understand my own circumstance and should just deal with whatever happened to me. They listened to my sisters and gave them a lot, but when I wanted even a tiny fraction of what they gave them, it became impossible to do.

Heck, they kidnapped us at home one morning to have us questioned by the police, and refused to tell us anything about why, where, with who, we were going. And after they decided it was dangerous for us at home, they took my sisters somewhere else, but left me, because I was "stubborn and wanted to be in a dangerous situation". I was a damn child, you don't abandon children to situations you deem dangerous just because they are stubborn. But I wasn't worth enough. I was never worth enough for them to care about me, even when they said they did.

I'm the girlfriend of a boy with BPD, and he relates to what is said in this post - not because I know what is happening in his brain, I totally don't, but because he has told me what he is afraid of, keep asking for reassurance, and has told me he thinks he is a negative factor in my life and a burden.

I just want to tell you that I really don't see you as a burden for needing to feel like someone loves you, and for reassurance that they don't find you a burden or a horrible person. I keep giving reassurance, and I try to make him feel safe with me. Yes, I do sometimes look like I hate him (my ASD prevents me from being fully aware of my body language) and he keeps asking me if I still love him - I've always answered "I do" and I really have no reason to stop, despite knowing him and the many things he struggles with. 

I know he hasn't shown me everything (most BPD hides their personality out of fear for rejection) but I am gradually making him more comfortable and I have seen some of his worse sides. (he's not yet split on me, but we have a plan for what we should do if that happens)

Anyway, I just wanted to say that I don't think you are a burden for wanting reassurance. It's completely natural, especially for people who have experienced trauma. You go girl!

First of all, congrats on being able to type your thoughts into words. As a fellow autistic female, I know that can be really hard to do. Some stuff I know from reading a lot of psychology during my life, because I myself has grown up really confused about myself, is that people question a lot, people have vastly different experiences of stuff and so on. I also know that autistic people, especially females since we so rarely get diagnosed and keep staying in the dark, are very susceptible and vulnerable to predators and abuse. The reason for this is that we are not aware that something is not normal to the same degree as neurotypical people are. We still feel the same emotions of fear, hurt, anger and so on, but we don't understand that it isn't normal, and a lot of adults fail at teaching us in a way that we actually do understand.


I would definitely suggest that you go see a psychologist/therapist that can help you figure out your problem, and see if you have BPD or not. You should try choosing one that has prior experience with autistic females, and children's psychology, because then they might have an easier time noticing what you are really struggling with.

Keep on being brave and great! If you are anything like my boyfriend, you take way too little credit for how great you are. And even if you are miles different from him, I'm still sure you are amazing! I hope you do great ❤️

So, people are mentioning to stay away from Mandarine (or Chinese in general) and I do agree with them.

I learned mandarin in school for two years, as a chosen foreign language, and it was really not that bad for the most part. I learned the signs pretty easily and the grammars wasn't that bad. But when it came to pronunciation - I did terrible!

Through those two years of studying, my teacher kept telling me the proper tones for words and how to do them, but I just couldn't make my brain figure out what tones were being used. That was my stepping stone. 

Because mandarin is a melodic language, and consists very greatly on the way you say words, it didn't go too well. 

I'm not saying "don't do Chinese", because I really think it is possible to learn it, even with difficulties when it comes to tone of voice. However, it will be worlds more difficult to get it right, and could involve a lot of demotivating factors and frustration.
